decisive_items: tender swelling in the outer half of the right breast with overlying warmth, erythema, and nipple retraction
skin fistula developed with pus extruding and an “orange peel” appearance of the overlying skin
Breast MRI revealed multiple oval and rounded lesions with irregular thick walls throughout the gland, extending to the skin, with peripheral enhancement
response.rationale: The clinical presentation and imaging findings are consistent with granulomatous mastitis, a rare inflammatory breast condition, with a more comprehensive set of supporting evidence compared to periductal mastitis.

rejected.why: Similar presentation but less specific to granulomatous lobular mastitis without distinct lobular involvement details.
Idiopathic granulomatous mastitis is a possibility but the evidence provided does not strongly differentiate it from granulomatous mastitis.
Idiopathic granulomatous lobular mastitis has some supporting evidence but it is less comprehensive compared to granulomatous mastitis.
